_comment: WCAG success criteria, hand-authored because there is no machine-readable source
that carries level and version together in a form worth depending on.
Scope: every Level A and AA criterion in WCAG 2.2, plus the criteria axe-core
actually references outside that set. The AAA entries are here because axe maps
rules to them and a reference that dropped those rules would be lying about what
the scanner does; 4.1.1 is here because it was removed in WCAG 2.2 and axe still
reports it, which is a fact worth stating rather than hiding.
`requires` is a plain-language summary, not a substitute for the specification.
Every entry links to the W3C's own Understanding document, which is the
authority. scripts/reference.js joins this against axe-core's rule metadata, and
test/wcag.test.js fails if axe references a criterion that is missing here.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.requires: Every image, icon, chart and control that is not text has a text alternative that serves the same purpose. Decorative images are marked so assistive technology can skip them.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.requires: Prerecorded audio has a transcript; prerecorded silent video has a transcript or an audio track describing it.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.requires: Prerecorded video with sound has captions covering speech and meaningful non-speech audio.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.requires: Prerecorded video has either an audio description of what is shown or a full text alternative.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.requires: Live audio content has real-time captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.requires: Prerecorded video has an audio description track — a text alternative is no longer sufficient at this level.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.requires: Structure conveyed visually is also conveyed in markup: headings are headings, lists are lists, table headers are associated with their cells, form fields with their labels.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.requires: When the order of content matters to its meaning, that order is available programmatically — the DOM order matches the reading order.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.requires: Instructions do not rely on shape, colour, size, position or sound alone. Not "click the round button on the right".

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.requires: Content does not lock itself to portrait or landscape unless a specific orientation is essential.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.requires: Fields collecting known personal information carry an autocomplete value, so a browser or assistive tool can fill or relabel them.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.requires: Colour is never the only way information is conveyed. A link inside body text needs an underline or another visual cue as well as a colour.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.requires: Audio that plays automatically for more than three seconds can be paused or muted independently of system volume.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.requires: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, or 3:1 for large text (18.66px bold, or 24px).

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.requires: Text can be enlarged to 200% without loss of content or function, and without horizontal scrolling to read a line.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.requires: Text is real text rather than a picture of text, unless the presentation is essential — a logo, for instance.

criteria.name: Contrast (Enhanced)
criteria.requires: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1, or 4.5:1 for large text.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.requires: Content reflows into a single column at 320 CSS pixels wide without requiring scrolling in two directions.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.requires: Interface components and meaningful graphics have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours — including the visible boundary of an input and the focus indicator.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.requires: No content or function is lost when a reader increases line height, and letter, word and paragraph spacing.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.requires: Content that appears on hover or focus can be dismissed, hovered over without vanishing, and stays visible until dismissed or no longer valid.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.requires: Everything can be operated from a keyboard alone, without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.requires: Keyboard focus can always be moved back out of a component using the keyboard.

criteria.name: Keyboard (No Exception)
criteria.requires: Everything is keyboard operable with no exception for functions that need path-dependent input.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.requires: Single-character shortcuts can be turned off, remapped, or are active only while a component has focus.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.requires: Time limits can be turned off, adjusted, or extended — with narrow exceptions such as a real-time event.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.requires: Movement, blinking or scrolling lasting more than five seconds can be paused, stopped or hidden. So can auto-updating content.

criteria.name: Interruptions
criteria.requires: Interruptions can be postponed or suppressed, except those involving an emergency.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.requires: Nothing flashes more than three times a second, unless it is below the general flash and red flash thresholds.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.requires: There is a way to skip repeated blocks of content — a skip link, or correct landmark structure.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.requires: Every page has a title that describes its topic or purpose.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.requires: Focus moves through the page in an order that preserves meaning and operability.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.requires: The purpose of each link is clear from its text, or from its text plus the surrounding context.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.requires: There is more than one way to reach a page within a set — search, a site map, or navigation.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.requires: Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of what they introduce.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.requires: The keyboard focus indicator is visible. Removing outlines without replacing them fails this.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
criteria.requires: The purpose of each link is clear from its text alone, without surrounding context.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.requires: When a component receives keyboard focus, it is not entirely hidden by other content — a sticky header or a cookie bar must not cover it.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.requires: Multi-point or path-based gestures have a single-pointer alternative, unless the gesture is essential.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.requires: An action is not completed on press-down; it can be aborted or undone before release.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.requires: A control's accessible name contains the text shown on it, so speech-input users can say what they see.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.requires: Anything triggered by device or user motion can also be operated by conventional controls, and motion actuation can be disabled.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.requires: Anything that uses a dragging movement has a single-pointer alternative that does not require dragging.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.requires: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or spaced so that a 24-pixel circle around each does not overlap another.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.requires: The page's default human language is set programmatically, so a screen reader pronounces it correctly.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.requires: Passages in a different language are marked with that language.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.requires: Receiving focus does not itself change the context — no dialog opening or navigation on focus alone.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.requires: Changing a setting does not automatically change context unless the user has been told it will.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.requires: Navigation repeated across pages appears in the same relative order each time.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.requires: Components with the same function are identified consistently across the set of pages.

criteria.name: Change on Request
criteria.requires: Changes of context happen only when requested, or a way to turn them off is available.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.requires: Help mechanisms repeated across pages — contact details, a help link, a chat widget — appear in the same relative order.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.requires: An input error is identified in text, and the item in error is described.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.requires: Labels or instructions are provided where input is required.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.requires: When an error is detected and a correction is known, it is suggested — unless doing so would compromise security.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.requires: Submissions with legal or financial consequences are reversible, checked, or confirmable before finalising.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.requires: Information already entered in a process is either auto-populated or available to select, rather than asked for again.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.requires: No cognitive function test — remembering a password, solving a puzzle — is required to authenticate, unless an alternative or a mechanism to assist exists. Pasting into a password field must work.

criteria.name: Parsing
criteria.requires: Markup has complete start and end tags, is nested correctly, and has no duplicate attributes or ids.
criteria.note: Removed in WCAG 2.2 as always satisfied by modern HTML parsing. axe-core still reports rules against it, so it appears here — a result citing 4.1.1 is not evidence of a 2.2 failure.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.requires: Every interface component exposes a name and a role, and its state and values can be read and set programmatically. This is the criterion custom widgets fail.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.requires: Status messages can be read by assistive technology without receiving focus — a live region, correctly used.
